input: Find bribery and corruption allegations involving Embraer, in Brazil and abroad

events.jurisdiction: United States and Brazil; conduct involving Argentina and the Dominican Republic
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; unnamed Argentine public official; Dominican Republic official Carlos Piccini; U.S. and Brazilian authorities
events.amount: US$3.4 million alleged payment in the Dominican Republic; underlying aircraft transactions reported at approximately US$92 million (Dominican Republic) and US$900 million list value (Argentina) (as of 2013-11-02)
events.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. and Brazilian authorities were investigating whether Embraer bribed officials in Argentina and the Dominican Republic to secure aircraft deals, including an alleged payment to a Dominican official through a Uruguayan shell company.

events.type: Brazilian civil inquiry / transnational corruption and money-laundering investigation
events.parties: Embraer S/A; current and former Embraer employees; Brazilian Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office (MPF); CVM
events.summary: An MPF portaria opened a civil inquiry based on criminal proceedings and investigative procedures alleging transnational active bribery and money laundering by current and former Embraer employees in aircraft sales to state entities in the Dominican Republic and Saudi Arabia, plus disguised payments to an Indian commercial representative; the inquiry focused on disgorgement of profits.

events.type: FCPA criminal enforcement / deferred prosecution agreement
events.jurisdiction: United States (Southern District of Florida); related Brazil, Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique and India conduct
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; U.S. Department of Justice
events.summary: The DOJ said Embraer entered a three-year DPA, admitted conspiracy to violate the FCPA’s anti-bribery and books-and-records provisions and willful failure to implement adequate internal accounting controls, and agreed to enhanced compliance, cooperation and an independent monitor.

events.type: FCPA civil enforcement / books-and-records and internal-controls settlement
events.jurisdiction: United States (SEC; Southern District of Florida)
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
events.amount: US$83.8 million disgorgement plus US$14.4 million prejudgment interest (more than US$98 million total; as of 2016-10-24)
events.summary: The SEC alleged that Embraer used third-party agents to route bribes to officials in the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia and Mozambique, concealed payments in false books and records, and used an improper accounting scheme in India; the settlement required disgorgement, interest and a three-year independent monitor.

events.type: Brazilian anti-corruption / disgorgement and securities settlement
events.parties: Embraer S.A.; Brazilian authorities; Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM)
events.amount: R$58 million disgorgement to a Brazilian federal fund plus R$6 million CVM penalties (as of 2016-10-24)
events.summary: The FCPA case record states that Embraer confirmed a settlement with Brazilian authorities requiring disgorgement of R$58 million and R$6 million in penalties to CVM in connection with the foreign-bribery conduct.

events.parties: 11 individuals in Brazil and 2 individuals in Saudi Arabia allegedly involved in Embraer-related misconduct; Embraer S.A. conduct described in the related resolution
events.summary: The DOJ reported that, with U.S. cooperation, Brazilian authorities charged 11 individuals over alleged involvement in Embraer’s Dominican Republic misconduct and Saudi authorities charged two individuals over alleged Saudi-related misconduct.

events.parties: Embraer S.A.; U.S. Department of Justice; U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
events.summary: The U.S. District Court dismissed the FCPA charges after finding Embraer had fully complied with its 2016 DPA; the company’s three-year monitorship had expired after a final report found its compliance program reasonably designed and implemented to detect and prevent anti-corruption violations.

events.parties: Embraer S.A.; Dominican and Mozambican authorities
events.amount: US$7 million paid to the Dominican Republic (as of the 2020 report)
events.summary: The DPA-completion report states that Embraer subsequently entered separate cooperation agreements with Mozambican and Dominican authorities, paid US$7 million to the Dominican Republic, and agreed to assist both countries with their ongoing investigations.

excluded_namesakes.name: Embraer RL
excluded_namesakes.reason: Related entity/bank account referenced in the FCPA case record, but excluded from the target entity because the requested subject is the parent/legal entity Embraer S.A.

output.assessment: Embraer presents high historical corruption risk: U.S. authorities said the company admitted multi-country bribery, false books and records, and internal-controls failures involving the Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique and India, while Brazilian authorities separately investigated and settled related conduct. The U.S. DPA was dismissed in 2020 after compliance completion, and Embraer’s 2025 sustainability indicators state that there were no confirmed corruption cases during 2025; however, the final outcomes for the individuals charged and the precise completion status of all foreign cooperation-related investigations were not verified in the pages opened. Sources: https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/embraer-agrees-pay-more-107-million-resolve-foreign-corrupt-practices-act-charges ; https://complianceconcourse.willkie.com/articles/news-alerts-2020-11-november-20201130-embraer-successfully-completes-dpa/ ; https://www.embraer.com/media/jebf3ij4/annual-sustainability-report-2025_-embraer.pdf
missing_fields: events[7].date (exact day/month for the Dominican Republic and Mozambique cooperation agreements)
events[5].status beyond the initial individual charges (final outcomes not verified)
post-2025 adverse-event status beyond the pages opened
